extracted.intended_audience: PolitiFact readers and general public interested in political fact-checking
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form fact-check article (PunditFact) that evaluates specific public claims by pundits or journalists, assigns a Truth‑O‑Meter rating, and explains the evidence behind that rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth‑O‑Meter rating (scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact’s Truth‑O‑Meter rating system (listed on the page): True, Mostly True, Half True, Mostly False, False, Pants on Fire, Full Flop, Half Flip, No Flip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page displays the Truth‑O‑Meter values and uses them to summarize the fact-check outcome (e.g., 'Read why that rates Half True.'). The rating is presented as the primary evaluative metric for the claim; readers can filter or browse items by rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explanation / justification for the assigned rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rated claim is accompanied by an explanation of why that particular Truth‑O‑Meter label was chosen (e.g., 'Read why that rates Half True.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checks give a narrative justification tying evidence to the rating. The page explicitly directs readers to explanations of the rating decisions rather than presenting ratings without context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of exact quoted wording and specific claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the subject actually said the precise words attributed to them (example on page: 'did O’Reilly’s never say "I was on the Falklands Islands"?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact-check examines transcripts, broadcasts, or published statements to confirm exact wording and whether the claim matches what was actually said; precise wording can determine rating (true vs. Half True, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and link to supporting sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-checks include sources and links that underpin the analysis (the page shows 'Our Sources — See individual fact-checks').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide primary sources (articles, broadcasts, transcripts) and secondary reporting as evidence. The page indicates readers can consult the listed sources for the basis of the rating; transparent sourcing is treated as essential to the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate competing or opposing claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple parties make conflicting accounts (here: Bill O’Reilly vs. David Corn/Mother Jones), the fact-check addresses and assesses claims from both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare statements and evidence from all involved parties; determine which parts of each party’s account are supported, contradicted, or ambiguous, and reflect that in the rating and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope to specific, verifiable factual questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes that the broader dispute is larger than a single fact-check and focuses on a specific verifiable question (whether O’Reilly said a particular phrase or claimed to be on the Falklands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrain each fact-check to discrete, checkable claims rather than attempting to adjudicate the entire controversy in one piece; state the limited question being evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metadata, tagging and filters to organize fact-checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides navigation and filtering options (Any Rating, Any Speaker, Any Date Range, categories, year filters) for browsing fact-checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify and tag fact-checks by rating, speaker, date, and category to make them discoverable and to contextualize individual checks within the broader archive.
